Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The device used for accurately measuring the emf of a primary cell is —
n equal resistances are connected first in series and then in parallel. The ratio R_s/R_p is —
questions.work:
R_s = nR; R_p = R/n.
R_s/R_p = nR ÷ (R/n) = n².

questions.q: To get the maximum resistance from three resistors, they should be connected —
A wire of length L and diameter D has the least resistance when its length and diameter are —
questions.work: R = ρL/A, A ∝ D². Doubling D makes A four times, so L and 2D gives R/4 — the smallest.

questions.work: Resistivity depends only on the material and temperature, not on the dimensions.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) At balance, a Wheatstone bridge satisfies P/Q = ______. (b) At balance, the current through the galvanometer is ______.
Match: (a) Resistors r, r in parallel — ? (b) Balanced Wheatstone bridge — ? [series combination / parallel combination / balanced Wheatstone bridge]
questions.answer:
(a) Parallel combination.
(b) Balanced Wheatstone bridge (the middle arm carries no current).

questions.q: Complete: a lamp is rated 40 W, 220 V. (a) Its resistance = ______. (b) Its safe current = ______.
State True or False: (a) Household appliances are connected in series. (b) A potentiometer draws no current from the cell at balance.
questions.answer:
(a) False — they are in parallel.
(b) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: The resistivity of a wire of length l and area A is 2 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. What is the resistivity of a wire of the same metal of length 2l and area 2A?
questions.answer: It is unchanged, 2 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. Resistivity is a property of the material (and temperature), not of its dimensions. (Its resistance R = ρl/A is also unchanged here.)

or.q: 8 V across a wire 3 cm long, area 2 cm², gives 0.15 A. Find its resistance and resistivity.

questions.q: A heating element is marked 220 V, 660 W. Calculate (i) the current and (ii) the resistance.
Name four factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends.
questions.answer: Length (R ∝ l), area of cross-section (R ∝ 1/A), nature of the material (resistivity ρ) and temperature.

or.q: Are household appliances connected in series or in parallel? Why?
or.answer: In parallel, so each gets the full mains voltage, each can be switched on or off independently, and a fault in one does not cut off the others.

questions.q: Why do free electrons in a conductor not produce magnetism when there is no p.d.?
questions.answer: Their thermal motion is random in all directions, so the average (drift) velocity is zero. There is no net current, and hence no net magnetic field.

questions.q: How does a potentiometer compare the emfs of two cells using sum and difference connections?
questions.answer:
Balance the cells aiding each other (E₁ + E₂ at length l₁) and opposing (E₁ − E₂ at length l₂).
(E₁ + E₂)/(E₁ − E₂) = l₁/l₂ ⇒ E₁/E₂ = (l₁ + l₂)/(l₁ − l₂).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: For the circuit with 10 Ω in series with 3 Ω and 6 Ω in parallel, across 12 V, find the equivalent resistance and the current.
questions.answer:
3 Ω ∥ 6 Ω = 3 × 6/(3 + 6) = 2 Ω.
Total R = 10 + 2 = 12 Ω.
I = V/R = 12/12 = 1 A (it divides as 2/3 A through 3 Ω and 1/3 A through 6 Ω).

or.q: A Wheatstone bridge with all arms r = 1 Ω is balanced and connected to 5 V. Find (a) the equivalent resistance and (b) the current in the arms.
or.answer:
Balanced ⇒ the middle arm carries no current and can be removed.
Two paths of r + r = 2 Ω each, in parallel ⇒ R = 1 Ω.
Total current = 5/1 = 5 A, so 2.5 A in each path (AB and DC).

questions.q: When a battery delivers 1 A its terminal p.d. is 9 V, and at 2 A it is 6 V. Find its internal resistance and emf.
questions.answer:
V = E − Ir.
9 = E − r and 6 = E − 2r.
Subtracting: r = 3 Ω; E = 9 + 3 = 12 V.

or.q: A wire has resistance 50 Ω at 20 °C and 50.5 Ω at 120 °C. Find the temperature coefficient of resistance.

questions.q: Derive an expression for the drift velocity of conduction electrons and relate it to current.
questions.answer:
In a field E an electron feels force eE and acceleration a = eE/m. Between collisions (average time τ) it gains velocity aτ, so v_d = eEτ/m.
In time t, the electrons in length v_d t pass a cross-section: charge = neAv_d t.
So I = neAv_d.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: State the principle of a potentiometer. With a circuit diagram, explain how it compares the emfs of two cells. Why is it better than a voltmeter?
questions.answer:
Principle: with a steady current through a uniform wire, the p.d. across any length is proportional to that length (V = kl).
Method: a driver cell sends a steady current through the wire AB. Cell E₁ (positive to A) is connected through a galvanometer and jockey; find the null point at l₁. Repeat with E₂ for l₂. Then E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂.
Advantage: at balance no current is drawn from the cell, so it measures the true emf; a voltmeter draws current and reads the terminal voltage, which is less than the emf.

questions.q: Two resistances R₁ and R₂ are connected to a V-volt battery, first in series and then in parallel. Derive the net resistance in each case and compare the currents.
questions.answer:
Series: the same current I flows through both. V = V₁ + V₂ = IR₁ + IR₂ = I(R₁ + R₂), so R_s = R₁ + R₂ and I_s = V/(R₁ + R₂).
Parallel: the same V across both. I = I₁ + I₂ = V/R₁ + V/R₂, so 1/R_p = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂, R_p = R₁R₂/(R₁ + R₂), and I_p = V(R₁ + R₂)/R₁R₂.
R_p is less than either resistance, so the parallel combination draws more current from the battery.
